questions.q: I remember ___ the door. (I'm sure I did it.)
questions.explanation: 'Remember + gerund' recalls a past action.

questions.q: Remember ___ your passport! (Don't forget to do it.)
questions.explanation: 'Remember + infinitive' is a reminder about a future action.

questions.q: She stopped ___ to answer the phone.
questions.explanation: 'Stop + gerund' means quit the activity.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He stopped to smoke last year.
questions.explanation: 'Stop + gerund' means he quit smoking.

questions.q: I tried ___ the window, but it was stuck.
questions.explanation: 'Try + infinitive' means attempt something difficult.

questions.q: Try ___ this cake — it's delicious.
questions.explanation: 'Try + gerund' means experiment to see what it's like.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I regret to tell him the secret.
I regret tell him the secret.
I regret told him the secret.
I regret telling him the secret.
questions.explanation: 'Regret + gerund' is sorry about a past action.

questions.q: I regret ___ you that I can't come.
questions.explanation: 'Regret + infinitive' announces bad news you are sorry to give.

questions.q: She went on ___ about her trip for an hour.
questions.explanation: 'Go on + gerund' means continue the same activity.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: After the introduction, she went on explaining the plan.
After the introduction, she went on explain the plan.
After the introduction, she went on to explain the plan.
After the introduction, she went to on explain the plan.
questions.explanation: 'Go on + infinitive' means move to a new activity.

questions.q: He forgot ___ the oven off.
questions.explanation: 'Forget + infinitive' means fail to do something.

questions.q: I'll never forget ___ the Eiffel Tower.
questions.explanation: 'Forget + gerund' recalls a memorable past event.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Did you remember locking the door?
Did you remember lock the door?
Did you remember locked the door?
Did you remember to lock the door?
questions.explanation: 'Remember + infinitive' asks about something you had to do.

questions.q: We stopped ___ some petrol.
questions.explanation: 'Stop + infinitive' means pause one action to do another.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She tried to call him, but he didn't answer.
She tried call him, but he didn't answer.
She tried calling him, but he didn't answer.
She tried called him, but he didn't answer.
questions.explanation: 'Try + gerund' means test a method to solve a problem.

questions.q: I mean ___ the report by Friday. (I intend to.)
questions.explanation: 'Mean + infinitive' expresses intention.

questions.q: This decision means ___ fifty people. (It involves...)
questions.explanation: 'Mean + gerund' describes what something involves.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I'm sorry to shout at you.
I'm sorry for shouting at you.
questions.explanation: 'Sorry for + gerund' apologises for a past action.

questions.q: I'm sorry ___ that you didn't get the job.
questions.explanation: 'Sorry + infinitive' expresses sympathy about news.

questions.q: The car needs ___.
questions.explanation: 'Need + gerund' has a passive meaning: it needs to be washed.
